k06.why: Two independent reports agree on the exhibition's name and venue. The year is inferred from the publication dates.

k07.name: 2021 Zhongzhou Jin-Yu (Golden Fish) Festival (1st ed.)
k07.creator: Students and faculty of the Institute of Arts Management and Entrepreneurship, NSYSU (advisor Xie Rong-feng)
k07.place: Zhongzhou, Qijin, Kaohsiung (ferry pier, fishing port, fish market, Ye ancestral hall, Yongzhou Theatre)
k07.summary: The Zhongzhou Jin-Yu Festival is an installation-art festival first held in 2021 in Zhongzhou, Qijin, Kaohsiung, by NSYSU's Institute of Arts Management and Entrepreneurship as part of its USR project 'The City is a Co-working Museum'. 'Jin' is the ferry pier and 'yu' is refuse; the homophone 'golden fish' links 'seeing the pier, knowing the fishery, scooping the refuse'. The first edition built 9 installations and a hidden spot across local culture, fishing culture and the environment (harbour marine debris), with a 'refuse-scooping' facility combining craftsman Zhuang Bi-fei's net-weaving; guided tours drew nearly 200 people over four days.
k07.editNote: The 1st edition (2021). On 2026-11-25 the former multi-edition entry was rewritten into one edition; the '2.0' (2024) is k110, under the Zhongzhou Jin-Yu Festival series.
k07.pedagogicalInsight: Graduate students bringing academic curatorial training (USR) into a fishing village overshadowed by heavy-shipbuilding stereotypes, re-reading its lanes through installation and tours, shows how a university can trigger local regeneration with one festival.
k07.why: Confirmed: Sina/Focus Media, 01today and NSYSU's official page corroborate the 2021 first edition, 9 installations plus a hidden spot, advisor Xie Rong-feng, the venues and the refuse-scooping facility, and nearly 200 visitors over four days.

k08.name: Kaohsiung Military Dependents' Village Trilogy
k08.creator: Hou Shu-tzu (video artist)
k08.place: Villages in Zuoying; Huangpu New Village, Fengshan
k08.summary:
The Kaohsiung Military Dependents’ Village Trilogy is a work by an artist who spent about eight years (2009–2017) visiting the new villages of Zuoying and Huangpu New Village in Fengshan, using residents’ oral accounts and images to record life and displacement memories amid the villages’ redevelopment and demolition.

The report is an excerpt from The Long Day Ends, built around the oral account of one Grandma Liu; the author interviewed her many times and invited her to return to the village.

The trilogy comprises We Meet Here, The Long Day Ends and Where Is Home?.
k08.selfDesc: The report is an excerpt from The Long Day Wanes, built around the oral account of one elderly woman, Grandma Liu, whom the author interviewed several times and invited back to her village. The trilogy comprises We Meet Here, The Long Day Wanes and Where Is Home.
k08.pedagogicalInsight: This is an artist’s personal work built over eight years of staying close to the place. Residents are interviewees, not co-creators, but it shows how “long companionship + oral accounts + images” builds credible local memory — through repeated returns and relationships rather than one-off collection. Note: it is work-oriented, not a participatory workshop.
k08.why: Verified: besides the Storm book excerpt, the VT Artsalon solo show 'The Long Day Closes' (2015) corroborates Hou Shur-tzy documenting, through images and residents' oral accounts, the lives of military-dependent households in Fongshan's Huangpu Village after they moved out, and the village's demolition, consistent with the 'Kaohsiung Military Village Trilogy' (a different show and outlet).

k09.name: Mudan Forest–Village–Sea Environmental Art and Design Camp
k09.creator: Department of Craft and Creative Design, National University of Kaohsiung; co-organized by Mudan Township Office and Mudan Township Community Development Association; in cooperation with Cheng Shiu University
k09.place: Xuhai, Mudan Township, Pingtung (Mudan Bay section of the Langqiao–Beinan Historic Trail)
k09.summary:
The Mudan Forest–Village–Sea Environmental Art and Design Camp is held at Xuhai, Mudan Township, Pingtung (the Mudan Bay section of the Langqiao–Beinan Historic Trail). The camp began in 2016, and 2024 was its 7th edition.

University staff and students worked with village residents to make three installations from driftwood and discarded fishing nets, on themes including ethnic integration and marine debris; resident Pan Kunlin taught students to weave discarded fishing nets.

The camp also developed an AR application presenting works from past editions, and a Mudan Township Office section chief said it has nurtured more than 15 amateur artists in the village.
k09.selfDesc: The report says resident Pan Kun-lin taught students to weave discarded fishing nets, and a Mudan Township Office section chief said the camp has trained more than 15 amateur artists from the tribe.
k09.pedagogicalInsight: The role reversal is notable: it is not an artist teaching residents, but a village resident teaching university students to weave discarded fishing nets. For teachers working across cultures or with local knowledge, it shows how “letting local people be the teachers” brings learners into the local context. Note: residents’ role in choosing themes is not reported.
k09.why: Pending: the Mudan 'Forest-Village-Sea' environmental art camp has only the 1111 campus-news source; other results are either the same outlet's university news or other Mudan projects, and one Liberty Times piece could not be read, so it is downgraded to pending.

k10.name: Street Museum (first edition: Zhongqin Village, Zhongzheng District)
k10.creator: Taipei Fine Arts Museum; in cooperation with Zhongqin Village, Zhongzheng District
k10.place: 228 Memorial Museum (results exhibition); Zhongqin Village, Zhongzheng District
k10.summary:
The Street Stories Museum is a project in which the Taipei Fine Arts Museum worked with residents of Zhongzheng District’s Zhongqin Village; the exhibition ran from 21 December 2019 to 22 March 2020, with results shown at the 228 Memorial Museum.

The project invited 34 senior residents to collect local memories and create works starting from paintings in the museum’s collection.

The results were shown together with works from the collection. The report says the project is planned to expand year by year to Taipei’s 12 districts, with goals including elder participation, intergenerational dialogue and local identity.
k10.selfDesc: The report says the project plans to expand to Taipei's 12 districts year by year, with goals including participation by older adults, intergenerational dialogue and local identity. The exhibition ran from December 21, 2019 to March 22, 2020.
k10.pedagogicalInsight: The project uses a painting from the museum collection as a starting point, giving elders a concrete way in, and then asks them to collect their own memories for making work, which lowers the barrier for non-artists. For teachers working with seniors, it models using an existing artwork to draw out personal memory. Note: the media of residents’ works are not reported.
k10.why: Verified: besides Taiwan News, 1% STYLE (LINE TODAY, 2025) also refers to the Taipei Fine Arts Museum's Zhongqin-li edition of 'Street Corner Museum' and its method of using collection paintings to prompt elders' local memories; note that piece dates the Zhongqin-li edition to 2019 (this entry says 2020), so fieldwork and the formal show may fall in different years.

k11.name: Turning Around in the Old City (Street Museum 2024)
k11.creator: Taipei Fine Arts Museum; artists Hsu Chia-chen, Tsui Kuang-yu and Lung Sze-liang
k11.place: Zhongshan Hall (border of Zhongzheng and Wanhua districts)
k11.summary:
Turning Around in Chengzhong is a 2024 Street Stories Museum project, on view until 2 March 2025 at Zhongshan Hall (on the boundary of Zhongzheng and Wanhua districts), with the everyday memories of Ximending and Chengzhong Market as its theme.

The project ran an old-photo card-game workshop and a mobile-phone video workshop, inviting residents and local shop owners to create; the artist took the role of a “counsellor”.

Local shops, residents and the artist thus took part in creating together.
k11.selfDesc: The report says local merchants, residents and artists took part in creating the work, with the artists acting as "counselors."
k11.pedagogicalInsight: The artist calls themself a “counsellor” rather than a creator, and that stance is itself a model for educators; low-threshold tools such as an old-photo card game and phone video let residents and shop owners tell their own stories. Both workshop formats can be borrowed directly.
k11.why: Verified: besides Islands of Museums, Mirror Media (2025-01-13) independently covered the 2024 'Street Corner Museum: City Turn', corroborating the Taipei Fine Arts Museum as host, the Chengzhong district/market theme and the card-game workshop made from shopkeepers' memory objects; the phone-video workshop detail rests on Islands of Museums.

k12.name: Freedom of Movement: Encountering the Last Scenes of Ankang Public Housing (Xinglong Social Housing Public Art Project)
k12.creator: Tomorrow Studio; artists Chen Po-yi, Fengjing Yinghua Creative Society, Liu Yi-yin and others
k12.place: Three vacant units in Ankang Public Housing, Wenshan District
k12.summary:
“Freedom of Movement: Encountering the Last Scenes of Ankang Public Housing” is a public art project for Xinglong social housing. From 8 March to 21 April 2024, before residents moved out, three vacant units in the Ankang public housing in Wenshan District were used for an exhibition.

Tomorrow Studio’s “Xinglong Little Living Room” was in residence for more than a year and ran activities such as baking cookies, drawing and small trips; residents took part in the collage for the main visual and contributed personal objects and stories.

The exhibition combined residents’ calligraphy, restored old photos, plaster hand casts and a documentary to show residents’ different choices about “moving” and “home”.
k12.selfDesc: The report says Tomorrow Studio's "Xinglong Living Room" had been on site for over a year, holding baking, drawing and small-trip activities. Residents took part in the key-visual collage and contributed personal objects and stories.
k12.pedagogicalInsight: The rhythm of this project is “relationships first, making later”: it stayed for over a year, building relationships through baking, drawing and small trips before holding an exhibition. A reminder for rushed workshops that relationships take time. Note: residents’ role in decisions is not reported.
k12.why: Verified: besides Islands of Museums, CNA (2024-03-21) reported the 'Freedom to Move' public-art show for the Xinglong social housing, corroborating an exhibition before the Ankang relocation, curation by Tomorrow Studio, and residents' stories shown via the documentary 'Monologue of Ruins'; items such as calligraphy, plaster hand-casts and photo restoration rest on Islands of Museums.

k13.name: We Are Home: Guangci Social Housing Public Art Project
k13.creator: Participating artists include Hsu Yung-hsu, Chiu Cheng-hung, Tseng Ling-li and Peng Kuan-chieh (the organizer's report does not state this explicitly)
k13.place: Guangci Social Housing complex, Xinyi District
k13.summary:
We Are Home is a public art project at the Guangci social housing estate, launched in 2020, with a results exhibition from 29 January to 10 February 2025 at the Guangci estate in Xinyi District.

The project builds relationships among residents through long-running series of workshops (private kitchens, book and recipe swaps, social prescriptions and more) and 18 installations; the report lists a private-kitchen project for women’s centre clients, herbal healing and a community garden, and a community flag co-created by residents.

Another work draws on the dreams told by more than ten residents.
k13.selfDesc: The report lists a private-kitchen project for women's center clients, herbal healing and a community garden, a community flag made together by residents, and works drawn from the dreams of more than ten residents told in interviews.
k13.pedagogicalInsight: The project uses everyday, ongoing activities such as private kitchens, book and recipe swaps and social prescriptions as the medium, so residents form relationships before there are artworks. For teachers working with communities, it shows an art project can begin with everyday things like eating together and swapping recipes, without talking about making art at first.
k13.why: Verified: besides Yahoo/Yam, CNA (2025-01-10) reported the 'We Are Home' public-art results show for the Guangci social housing, corroborating the site, curation by He Lei Art (Wu Hui-chen), 18 installations plus the 'Museum of Migration', over 200 community workshops before the show, and residents' stories as material; specific strands such as the private kitchen, book/recipe swaps and 'social prescriptions' rest on the original report.

k14.name: Sundays Unseen: One-Forty International Migrant Photography Award Exhibition
k14.creator: National Theater & Concert Hall "2026 Autumn Arts Festival" and the One-Forty International Migrant Photography Award; migrant worker photographers from Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand working in Taiwan
k14.place: Gate 2, National Theater (21-1 Zhongshan S. Rd., Taipei)
k14.summary:
The Sunday-Only Scenery international migrant-worker photography award has run since 2019; 2026 is its 7th edition. Based on Photovoice theory, it is exhibited at the National Theater and Concert Hall for the first time. The special exhibition is at Gate 2 of the National Theater, from 20 September to 29 November 2026, free, daily 12:00–20:00.

It shows works by migrant workers in Taiwan who recorded their own lives with phones or cameras; the photographers decide what to shoot and how they want to be understood. The exhibition starts from the question “what if you had only one day off a month”, and entries came from migrant workers from Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand.

It presents the 2026 winners and selections from past years in three parts — “Limited Space | Survival Mission”, “Limited Time | Soul Relaxation” and “Limited Self | Becoming Yourself” — with themes of labour, diaspora, identity and memory, and ends with a planned “migrant issues reading list”.
k14.selfDesc: The report says the award has run since 2019, 2026 is its seventh edition, it is based on Photovoice theory, and this is its first showing at the National Theater & Concert Hall. The show presents the 2026 winners and selections from past years, with entries from migrant workers from Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand; it has three sections (Limited Space | Survival Mission, Limited Time | Relaxing the Mind, Limited Self | Becoming Yourself), covers labor, diaspora, identity and memory, and ends with a reading list on migrant-worker issues. Open daily 12:00–20:00.
k14.pedagogicalInsight: This is a representative Photovoice case: migrant workers decide what to photograph and how they want to be seen, while the award only provides a frame and one question (what if you had only one day off a month). For teachers who want learners to “hold the voice”, it is the cleanest model: the facilitator poses the question and participants answer for themselves.
k14.why: Previously confirmed by human review (October 2026). A LINE TODAY report and Marie Claire both mention the NTCH–One-Forty collaboration, but the dates, venue and edition number still rest on one source; the Vogue and NCAF pages could not be read.

k15.name: "Cool Symbiosis" Gender Exhibition
k15.creator: Museum of National Taipei University of Education; 11 artists and groups including Liu Yu and Lee Mao Huan
k15.place: Museum of National Taipei University of Education
k15.summary:
“Cool Symbiosis” is a gender-themed exhibition at the MoNTUE (Museum of National Taipei University of Education) from 22 July to 17 September 2023.

Eleven groups of artists worked with scientists and other actors, using stories of biodiversity and gender diversity to help visitors understand and accept sexual minorities.

The report says the show hopes visitors will come to know the many dimensions of biology and gender.
k15.selfDesc: The report says the exhibition hopes audiences will come to see the diversity of biology and gender.
k15.pedagogicalInsight: This show has no community participation; it is an issue exhibition meant to help visitors understand and accept. But it models using “biodiversity” as an analogy for “gender diversity”, placing a sensitive issue in more neutral scientific language — one way in for teachers discussing gender. Note: it is curation-led, not participatory.
k15.why: Verified: besides PTS, Taiwan News reported the MoNTUE show 'Queer-Symbiosis' with 11 artist groups, and the Taiwan Contemporary Art Archive and C-LAB magazine also document it, so the core (MoNTUE, 11 groups, gender/biodiversity themes) is corroborated across sources.

k16.name: ADAM Artists' Laboratory
k16.creator: Taipei Performing Arts Center (curator River Lin); 2019: 12 artists from 12 countries; 2026: 7 artists from Indonesia, Vietnam, Hong Kong, the Philippines, Australia, Japan and Taiwan
k16.place: 2019: Longshan Temple area in Wanhua and Dadaocheng Theater; 2026: Manila (August residency) and Taipei (October residency and meeting)
k16.summary:
The Asian Contemporary Performance Network assembly (ADAM) has been an international artist residency and exchange platform run by the Taipei Performing Arts Center since 2017. The 2019 report says its theme was “community (and) art”, concerned with the social turn of contemporary art.

In 2019 (the 3rd edition), 12 international artists were in residence in Taipei for about four weeks (from 22 July), visiting communities such as LGBTQ people, migrant workers, homeless people and Indigenous peoples; sites included the Longshan Temple area in Wanhua and the Dadaocheng Theatre.

The 2019 annual meeting ran 15–18 August. In 2026 (the 9th edition) it became a Manila–Taipei two-city residency under the theme “Relations Pending, Art Unfinished”, held in Taipei on 15–18 October around the concept of a “laundry day”, with city walks.
k16.selfDesc: The 2019 report says the theme was "Community (and) Art", concerning the social turn in contemporary art; the residency began July 22 for four weeks and the annual meeting ran August 15–18. The 2026 official pages say the 9th edition is held every two years (since 2025) with three strands (Artist Lab, New Work Exploration, Exchange & Forum), runs October 15–18, uses the concept of "Laundry Days", and includes city walks in Taipei (Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, National Palace Museum, Shung Ye Museum of Formosan Aborigines, Machangding Memorial Park, etc.).
k16.pedagogicalInsight: This is an international exchange and residency platform for artists; communities are visited and exchanged with, not co-creators, so its direct value for classroom teaching is limited — it is more an administrative model of how to design a residency and exchange. Note: in 2019 artists and communities visited and exchanged, they did not create together.
k16.why: Previously confirmed by human review (October 2026). The 2019 year and third-edition status are corroborated by Taiwan News and a Global Gender report; the 2026 edition is described by Taipei Performing Arts Center and National Performing Arts Center pages, which differ slightly in detail.

k17.name: "Interwoven": Co-creating the Museo Aero Solar
k17.creator: New Taipei City Museum of Art; artist Tomás Saraceno; a community college linking schools and community groups in the Sanying–Tushu area
k17.place: New Taipei City Museum of Art (Yingge District)
k17.summary:
“Weaving the Universe Together” is a 2026 exhibition at the New Taipei City Art Museum (Yingge), on view 21 March – 6 September, with works dated 2023–2026. “Museum of Solar Flight” is an important extension project of the show, combining art-making, environmental thinking and public participation.

Members of the public collectively collaged and painted recycled plastic bags to help make a floating sculpture that rises with solar heat. The report says the project has developed since 2007 and been carried out in more than 30 countries, and this is its first time in Taiwan; the work belongs to the artist’s Aerocene project, and the Taiwan version includes works by Taiwanese participants as well as results previously shown in Thailand and Korea.

The museum also held lift-off experiments, and the work was shown in the “Weaving the Universe Together” exhibition.
k17.selfDesc: The report says the project has developed since 2007 and been carried out in more than 30 countries, and that this is its first time in Taiwan. The museum's page calls it an important extension of the exhibition, combining artistic creation, environmental thinking and public participation; exhibition coverage says the work belongs to the artist's Aerocene project, and the Taiwan version includes works by Taiwanese participants and results from earlier showings in Thailand and Korea.
k17.pedagogicalInsight: The project uses “open source — everyone makes one big thing that flies” as its draw, with a low threshold and a high sense of achievement. But it is the Taiwan version of an international project and its issue (environmental sustainability) did not grow from local context; in IBAE terms (“from context”) it is a content-first example, useful for contrast and discussion.
k17.why: Previously confirmed by human review (October 2026). The newly added museum page, Marie Claire, Yam and the international project page agree on the work's name, exhibition dates, citizen co-creation and the project's 2007 origin; no source describes the Taiwan co-creation process in detail.

k18.name: The Futurists: Living Practices for Future Cities
k18.creator: Curated by Haobanshe; 9 artists and groups including Wei Chao-yi, Liu Kai-chen, Chang Cheng-chun, Hsu Chia-chen and Wei Theatre
k18.place: Beitun Social Housing; Wuqi Sanmin Social Housing
k18.summary:
Futurists: Living Exercises for Future Cities is public art shown in October 2025 at the Beitun social housing and the Wuqi Sanmin social housing.

Residents provided old photos and life stories, a theatre workshop invited them to talk about “moving house”, and spaces not usually open to the public, such as the rooftop and mailbox areas, were opened.

The source for this case is a critical essay by the curator, who questions measuring community empowerment by KPIs and asks what public art leaves residents after the project ends.
k18.selfDesc: This is a critical essay by a curator. The author questions measuring community empowerment by KPIs and asks what the public art will leave residents after the project ends.
k18.pedagogicalInsight: The source is the curator’s own critical essay, which asks the question an educator should ask: once the project ends and the KPIs come down, what does public art leave residents? A reminder for anyone running community projects: do not treat “how many events, how many people” as proof of empowerment.
k18.why: Confirmed: besides The Reporter's on-site critique, an official Taichung City (Housing Development Engineering Office) news release (2025-10-18) and the Artemperor exhibition page independently corroborate the core facts — organized by the Taichung City Housing Development Engineering Office, curated and run by Haobanshe, shown at Beitun and Wuqi Sanmin social housing, 17-26 Oct 2025, 9 artists/groups, with artists doing prior in-residence fieldwork — matching The Reporter, so it is upgraded to confirmed. The resident-participation details (old photos and life stories, a theater/script-reading workshop on 'moving house', opening rooftops and mailbox areas) still rest mainly on The Reporter alone. (Daily source expansion, 2026-11-14)

k19.name: Bu Long Project (Open, and next Art Experiment Field)
k19.creator: Indigenous Peoples Cultural Foundation (organizer); Taoyuan City Indigenous Peoples Affairs Dept. (partner); KIRI Indigenous Peoples Cultural and Creative Park (co-organizer); artists Ali Istanda (Hu Chia-yu), Siyat Moses (Juan Yuan-min) and maya' a taboeh hayawan (Luo Yuan)
k19.place: KIRI Indigenous Peoples Cultural and Creative Park, Qingpu (Zhongli and Dayuan districts, Taoyuan)
k19.year: 2026 (official page: 1 Jul–31 Aug; earlier reports: residency Jun–Aug, Taiwan Design Expo in September)
k19.summary:
Bu-Long Project (Open, and next art lab) is a 2026 residency and event series at the KIRI International Indigenous Cultural and Creative Park in Qingpu, Taoyuan. The official page gives 1 July – 31 August, while earlier reports say a June–August residency; the two may refer to different phases and still need confirming with the organiser.

Three young Indigenous artists were in residence in Qingpu and ran free participatory workshops using local materials such as ponds, temple incense ash and fallen leaves, recalling pond memories lost to development; one artist guided elders at a community health station to turn pond-life experiences into printmaking material.

The official programme also includes a “Qingpu Sensing Database” city exploration: participants pick up an Exploration Notebook, visit old settlements, ponds and the Laojie River, collect stamps and file them on the 4th floor.
k19.selfDesc: The report says visitors could book to create with the artists, and one artist guided elders at a day-care center to turn their pond-side life experiences into printmaking material. The official page frames the programme as re-seeing, sensing and reading Qingpu, covering land memory, urban change and the history of different groups living together; visitors pick up an Exploration Notebook, collect stamps and archive them on the 4th floor, and workshops require registration. Listed workshops are Bu Long Project: Scales Erupting (Hu), Rmdax Memory Developing: Tetra Pak Printmaking (Juan) and ki:ki:im Wasteland Exploration: Body Messages (Luo).
k19.pedagogicalInsight: The artist guiding elders to turn “pond-life experience” into printmaking material is a way of turning older people’s everyday memories into creative content; the “Qingpu Sensing Database / Exploration Notebook / stamp-and-file” city-walk design can also be borrowed directly as a walking worksheet.
k19.why: Previously confirmed by human review (October 2026). Two newly added official pages agree with earlier reports on the organizer, the three artists, the venue and the workshops; the residency/programme dates differ between sources, and the September exhibition is not confirmed by the new sources.

k20.name: Symbiotic Window Poem: Public Art Co-creation Workshop
k20.creator: Taoyuan City Government; artist Wu Chien-yi; executed by Youmi Integrated Marketing
k20.place: Fu'an Park, rear of Taoyuan Railway Station
k20.year: 2026 (workshops Jun 26 and 28, inferred from report dates)
k20.summary:
Symbiotic Window Poems is a public art co-creation workshop at Fuan Park behind Taoyuan Railway Station, held in 2026 on 26 and 28 June (dates inferred from the report). The area behind the station has long been a gathering place for migrant workers and new immigrants, forming a Southeast Asian commercial area; the workshop takes multiculturalism and migration as its theme.

The workshop recruited 45 participants to share stories about Taoyuan, the station or “movement”, and asked them to bring food packaging as creative material.

The outcome is a public artwork using the suitcase as its image.
k20.selfDesc: The report says migrant workers and new immigrants have long gathered at the rear of the station, forming a Southeast Asian commercial area, and that the work's themes are multiculturalism, mobility and migration.
k20.pedagogicalInsight: Asking participants to “bring a piece of food packaging” as creative material is a clever way to make personal experiences of movement and migration concrete; talking about “movement” through everyday carried objects such as suitcases and packaging is closer to life than talking about immigration policy. Note: whether participants included migrant workers themselves is not reported.
k20.why: Pending: the 'Symbiotic Window-Scene Poem' co-creation workshop is reported only by ETtoday (an exact-name search found no second independent source), so it is downgraded to pending. On 2026-11-14 a further search by exhibition name and by artist Wu Chien-yi, Fu'an Park and 'suitcase' still found no second independent source (hits were mostly other works by the artist, not this workshop), so it remains pending. (Daily source expansion, 2026-11-14)

k21.name: Picture-Book Creation Course for New Immigrants and Migrant Workers (Words, Paint, See)
k21.creator: National Immigrants' Life Aesthetics Museum (the report elsewhere writes "National Hsinchu Life Aesthetics Museum"; the two are inconsistent)
k21.place: Participants from New Taipei, Taoyuan and Hsinchu; awards held at Beida Park, Hsinchu City
k21.summary:
The picture-book course for new immigrants and migrant workers, “Talk · Draw · See”, is a 2019 art education course; learners came from New Taipei, Taoyuan and Hsinchu, and the awards ceremony was held at Beida Park in Hsinchu City.

The course recruited new immigrants and foreign migrant workers from 8 countries, who used picture books to express memories of home and life in Taiwan, on themes including childhood memories, cross-border marriage, hometown scenery and cultural differences.

The course produced more than 30 works and held an awards ceremony.
k21.selfDesc: The report says participants came from 8 countries, and themes included childhood memories, cross-border marriage, hometown scenery and cultural differences.
k21.pedagogicalInsight: The course uses picture books as the vehicle for new immigrants and migrant workers to draw their hometowns and their experiences in Taiwan; the barrier is low, yet it can handle private themes such as cross-border marriage and cultural difference. With learners who do not share a language, images are often the best common language. Note: the venue and instructors are not reported.
k21.why: Verified: besides Taiwan News (2019), NOWnews (2022) reported that the 'Speak-Draw-See' picture-book project is run by the Ministry of Culture's Hsinchu Living Arts Center since 2019, corroborating the recruitment of new residents and migrant workers, picture books expressing homeland memory and life in Taiwan, and the works and awards (a later year of the same project).

k22.name: 2019 Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival (1st edition) — 'All the Time in the World'
k22.creator: Organised by the Hakka Affairs Council; overall curatorial-design director Wu Han-chung; curators incl. Lin Shun-lung, Akibo Lee, Lin Yi-hua
k22.place: Hakka villages along Provincial Highway 3 (across 5 counties, about 10 townships)
k22.summary: The first Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival was held in 2019 by the Hakka Affairs Council, themed 'All the Time in the World', along the Hakka villages of Provincial Highway 3 across five counties and about ten townships. The first edition gathered 50-70-odd artists and teams, about 50 works and nearly a hundred cultural activities; local schoolchildren took part in gathering and making local crafts such as fan-palm fans and blessing brooms. It won a 2020 Good Design Award.
k22.selfDesc: Reports note local schoolchildren took part in gathering and making local crafts; the first edition spanned five counties with about 100 activities and 50-70-odd artists and teams.
k22.editNote: The first edition (2019) of the Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival. On 2026-11-25, at the user's request, the previously blended 2019/2023 entry was split: this entry covers the 2019 first edition; the 2023 second edition is k85; both sit under the 'Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival' series. Artist counts differ across sources (50-odd vs 70-odd), both noted.
k22.pedagogicalInsight: In a large festival, having schoolchildren gather and make local crafts passes Hakka village skills to the next generation. But the balance of 'artist-led' versus 'children's participation' differs greatly; a caution that festival scale does not equal depth of participation.
k22.why: Confirmed: Taiwan News (2019) reports the first edition's opening and the Route 3 scale; NOWnews recaps the first edition's 70-odd artists, 50 works, 100 activities and the 2020 Good Design Award; artist counts differ across sources, both noted.

k23.name: 2025 Chenglong Wetlands Environmental Art Festival — 'The Land is Like a Flower'
k23.creator: Chenglong Community Development Association, Kouhu, Yunlin (2025 organiser); resident artists incl. Li Kuei-chih, Tung Yu-hao, Chang Kuo-yao
k23.summary: The 2025 Chenglong Wetlands Environmental Art Festival, themed 'The Land is Like a Flower', was held after a five-year break. The Chenglong Wetlands in Kouhu, Yunlin, formed through land subsidence and seawater intrusion. Organised by a team from the Chenglong Community Development Association, artists were in residence for three weeks (7-27 Apr 2025); residents, volunteers and resident artists completed four works together from local materials such as woven bamboo and driftwood, with performances and a market.
k23.selfDesc: Reports note the festival returned after a two-year break; a three-week residency (7-27 Apr 2025) completed four works with volunteers.
k23.editNote: The 2025 edition of the Chenglong Wetlands festival. On 2026-11-25 the previously blended 2022/2025 entry was split: this entry covers 2025; the 2010 first edition is k86, 2017 is k87, the 2022 return is k88, all under the series.
k23.pedagogicalInsight: Residents, volunteers and resident artists making installations together from bamboo and driftwood is a classic three-way co-creation; making environmental art on a wetland formed by subsidence and seawater intrusion puts the issue literally underfoot - a clear 'from place' example.
k23.why: Confirmed: Yam News (2025) and PTS 'Our Island' independently corroborate the 2025 'Land is Like a Flower' edition returning after five years, organised by the community association, with residents and resident artists co-creating.

k24.name: Again: Chiayi Rural Art Actions
k24.creator: Curator Hsiang Chia-hung; in cooperation with community development associations, schools and cultural-history foundations
k24.place: Townships across Chiayi County (this year, townships in the Beigang River basin)
k24.year: Since 2022 (the report calls this year the fourth)
k24.summary:
Again: Chiayi Rural Art Action has run since 2022; the report calls this year its 4th, covering townships across Chiayi County (this year the townships of the Beigang River basin).

Artists made repeated visits to rural Chiayi and co-created 13 works with residents aged 6 to 90, responding to local culture; most works respond to “ethnic groups and migration”, with mentions of Shanglin’s sugar-making memory and migrant workers.

The works will be shown at the 2026 Taiwan Lantern Festival.
k24.selfDesc: The report says most works respond to "ethnicity and migration," and mentions Shanglin's sugar-making memories and foreign migrant workers. The works will be shown at the 2026 Taiwan Lantern Festival.
k24.pedagogicalInsight: Creating with residents aged 6 to 90 and responding to local memories of ethnic groups and migration shows what intergenerational co-making can be. But note that the source is a county-government advertorial with only positive claims, so the real depth of resident participation should be discounted.
k24.why: Verified: the original Global Views piece was an advertorial and not independent; PTS 'Our Island' (2025-03-19) independently corroborates that the action was curated by Hsiang Chia-hung, with artists visiting Chiayi rural communities and co-creating with elders. The number of works varies by source (Global Views 13, PTS 17), as noted.

k25.name: Penghu Drifting Art Museum (Youth Patrol Beach Cleanup)
k25.creator: Youth patrol led by Tang Tsai-ling (studio founder); resident artist Tai Shuo-yi
k25.place: "Drifting Art Museum" at the Houliao Visitor Center
k25.summary:
Penghu Drifting Art Museum is the “Drifting Art Museum” at the Houliao Visitor Centre in Penghu in 2025, grown out of a youth patrol team’s beach cleanups.

Beach cleaning has gradually become a way for residents to show love for their home, and the team has done environmental education for about 10 years; after cleanups, the youth patrol turns marine debris into installations.

The works are placed in the Houliao Visitor Centre to make visitors think about ocean waste. The report does not say whether residents took part in making the works.
k25.selfDesc: The report says beach cleaning has gradually become a way residents show love for their home, and the team has done environmental education for about 10 years. It does not say whether residents took part in making the works.
k25.pedagogicalInsight: Turning marine debris picked up on beach cleanups directly into exhibits merges environmental action and making, so visitors see where rubbish comes from. For environmental-education teachers, it models a full cycle of action, collection, remaking and display. Note: whether residents took part in making the works is not reported.
k25.why: Verified: besides PTS, the Commercial Times (2025-08-25) corroborates the Houliao 'Drift Museum', kayak beach-cleaning collecting marine debris, and the debris remade into art; however it centres on the artist Tang Tang (Sea Drift Lab) with the Penghu scenic-area administration, not the 'youth patrol', so the two may be different participants or editions of the same 'Drift Museum', and which group did the cleanup is unresolved.

k26.name: Art Moving Communities (Kinmen and Penghu)
k26.creator: National Tainan Living Art Center (Ministry of Culture); co-organized with the Kinmen and Penghu county cultural bureaus; project lead Wu Mali
k26.place: Kinmen: Gugang, Hudong; Penghu: Dachi, Houliao, Dingwan, Hudong, Jiangjun and other communities
k26.summary:
Art Turning Communities is a 2025 (ROC year 114) programme in which artists took up residence in communities in Kinmen (Gugang, Hudong) and Penghu (Dachi, Houliao, Dingwan, Hudong, Jiangjun and others). The report says the programme emphasises the community as its main body and has run in seven southern counties and cities for five years.

Artists worked with residents: planning a performance with a paper-craft master, firing pottery with residents, and interviewing elders to preserve folk songs.

The exact residency sites and dates of each artist are not reported.
k26.selfDesc: The report says the program puts the community at the center and has run for 5 years across seven counties and cities in the south.
k26.pedagogicalInsight: Working with local practitioners such as a paper-craft master, potters and folk-song elders, rather than parachuting contemporary art into a community, respects local skills; for teachers working on local culture, the point is to find the community’s masters first. Note: the source is an advertorial in the Ministry of Culture’s name and leans toward the official account.
k26.why: Confirmed (core): besides the Ministry of Culture advertorial, an independent CNA staff report (2025-06-03, news/acul) corroborates this case's core — the 'Art Moving Communities' program run by the Ministry of Culture's National Tainan Living Art Center, a 2025 (ROC 114) residency at the county-designated historic 'Dong Yun-yao Mansion' in Gugang, Kinmen, with artists (Lin Huang-di and Chen Hsin-cheng) working with residents (collecting and illustrating residents' life stories, borrowing household objects such as electric fans) — agreeing with the advertorial on the program, organizer, year, and Kinmen community residency with resident collaboration, so it is upgraded to confirmed. However, the specific examples listed here (co-planning a performance with a paper-craft master, firing pottery with residents, interviewing elders to preserve folk songs), the Penghu communities and project lead Wu Mali still rest on the single advertorial source. (Daily source expansion, 2026-11-14)

k27.name: Hualien Jump Wave Arts Festival: "Planet Burst"
k27.creator: Organizer not stated in the report; artists include Iyo Kacaw, Chang Pu-teng, Tu Wei-cheng and Chen Cheng-tao
k27.place: Hualien County Stone Sculpture Museum; Tongli tribe
k27.summary:
Hualien Jump Wave Art Festival “Planet Burst” is a 2024 exhibition at the Hualien Stone Sculpture Museum and Tongli Village, themed on the Hualien earthquake and exploring how people live with earthquakes and heal.

Tu Wei-cheng invited residents to bring post-quake objects for rubbing, and Chen Cheng-tao worked with adults and children of the village to assemble post-quake mountain views from Lego.

Income from showing the Lego works will be donated to rebuild the local church.
k27.selfDesc: The report says the exhibition explores how people live with earthquakes and heal, and income from showing the LEGO works will be donated to rebuild a local church.
k27.pedagogicalInsight: “Bring an object from after the quake to rub” and “build post-quake mountains from Lego” turn earthquake trauma into something to make; letting children handle disaster with Lego is a very practical healing design. For teachers dealing with trauma, it shows using concrete objects and play media instead of talking about the disaster directly. Note: how residents decided the content of works is not reported.
k27.why: Verified: besides PTS, CNA (2024-10-22) reported the 3rd PALAFANG Hualien Jumping Wave Art Festival 'Planet Burst Observatory', corroborating the Hualien County Cultural Affairs Bureau as host, the 0403-earthquake theme and Tu Wei-cheng's 'Earthquake Museum'; the details 'Tu having residents make rubbings from post-quake objects' and 'Chen Cheng-tao building a Lego post-quake landscape' rest on PTS (CNA does not mention them).

k28.name: Meeting of Styles (Graffiti in Gouzaiwei, Hualien)
k28.creator: Invited by Hualien City Office; MOS Hualien lead Huang Hung-shun; over a hundred graffiti artists
k28.summary:
Meeting of Styles is a two-day graffiti event starting on 19 October 2024 in the old quarter of Gouziwei, Hualien City.

Hundreds of graffiti artists painted about 50 wall works; the township office coordinated residents to provide old walls and roller shutters, and many works took the walls that collapsed in the earthquake as their subject.

The organiser hopes the works will help people remember the earthquake and restore confidence, and the mayor hopes the old quarter will become a street-culture landmark for young people.
k28.selfDesc: The report says the lead hopes the works help people remember the earthquake and restore confidence, and the mayor hopes the old district will become a landmark of youth street culture.
k28.pedagogicalInsight: Residents mainly lent their walls rather than co-creating, so participation is shallow; but “taking the walls that collapsed in the quake as subject” turns traces of disaster directly into a place for making — an example of landscape combined with trauma. Its direct reference value for educators is limited; it is closer to a city-regeneration or tourism case.
k28.why: Verified: besides PTS, LiFTED (2024-10-22) corroborates the 2024 Hualien Meeting of Styles, over 50 walls turned into graffiti, and the magnitude-7.2 Hualien earthquake as backdrop; the details 'Goujhaiwei old district', 'the district office arranging residents' walls and shutters' and 'using collapsed post-quake walls as subject' rest on PTS (LiFTED gives no location detail).

k29.name: Damp Palimpsest: Neighborhood Art Action
k29.creator: Humanities Innovation and Social Practice Program (HISP), National Taiwan Ocean University; Arts Commission at Sunrise First Sight Cafe; young creators
k29.place: Public spaces of Zhishan Building, Ren'ai District; First Sight Cafe
k29.summary:
Damp Palimpsest is a neighbourhood art action held from 22 August to 20 September 2026 in the public spaces of the Zhishan Building in Ren’ai District, Keelung, and at Chujian Café.

Young creators went to the Kanzaiding and consignment-shop (weituohang) districts to gather material; the team used the Lumbung (shared rice barn) method, sharing local cultural materials and fieldwork experience with the creators, and coordinated the space with the building’s management committee.

The works were shown in a community gallery converted from the building’s public space, depicting the sewing trade, fish market and railway memories of Keelung’s old town.
k29.selfDesc: The report says the team used the Lumbung (shared rice barn) approach, sharing local cultural materials and field experience with the creators, and coordinated the space with the building's management committee.
k29.pedagogicalInsight: The team used the Lumbung (shared rice barn) method to share fieldwork materials with creators; this “share first, then create separately” model is a mechanism teachers leading group projects can borrow. Note: residents were mainly people the creators drew material from, and the degree of co-creation is not reported.
k29.why: Verified: besides the 1111 report, the China Daily News (Chinese News Cloud, reporter Yang Yao-hua, 2026-08-25, republished on Yahoo) independently covers the 'Damp Palimpsest' action, confirming that NTOU's HISP program and the Sunrise First Sight Cafe's 'Arts Commission' jointly launched it, that young creators gathered material in the Kanzaiding and pawnshop district, and that it ran in the 'community gallery' in Zhishan Building and the cafe through Sep 20 — upgraded to verified. (daily source expansion, 2026-11-15)

k31.name: Guantian Has Monsters!!! The Ponds and Legends of Guantian (Art Goes to the Countryside)
k31.creator: Department of Art History, Tainan National University of the Arts (advisor Hsu Yuan-ta); in cooperation with teachers and students of Guantian Junior High School
k31.place: Guantian Junior High School, Guantian District (art space on the 2nd floor of the school store; the venue is stated only by the Liberty Times)
k31.summary:
There Are Monsters in Guantian!!! The Ponds and Legends of Guantian is a 2023–2024 art-to-village project by a team from the Department of Art History at the Tainan National University of the Arts at Guantian Junior High School in Guantian District, under the Ministry of Education’s Higher Education Sprout Project theme of fulfilling social responsibility; the venue is the art space on the 2nd floor of the school shop.

The team led Guantian Junior High students, first using drama classes to get to know the monster legends of the Guantian ponds, then drawing characters such as the snail spirit, loach spirit, black dog blood and Qing soldiers and placing them in a Guantian scene hand-drawn by the university team.

The results were turned into an exhibition. The content covers the ponds’ irrigation and flood-control functions and the relation between legends and hydrology and geography, aiming to help students and locals rediscover fading local legends and to give rural students aesthetic education.
k31.selfDesc: The reports say the project falls under the Ministry of Education's Higher Education Sprout Project, "social responsibility" strand. It covers the ponds' irrigation and flood-prevention functions and the relation between the legends and local hydrology and geography, aiming to help students and locals rediscover fading local legends and to give rural students aesthetic education.
k31.pedagogicalInsight: Using a drama class to let students “enter” the monster legends of the Guantian ponds, then drawing characters and placing them in a shared scene for an exhibition, turns almost-forgotten local legends into students’ own creations — a good mix of local knowledge and aesthetic education that can serve directly as a template for local-culture courses.
k31.why: Three reports (including the university's own e-newsletter) agree on the project name, partners and content; the exhibition dates are reported inconsistently.

k30.name: "Painting, 25": Puli After the 921 Earthquake
k30.creator: New Homeland Cultural and Educational Foundation; 11 artists including Chu Chi-chu, Sun Shao-ying and Liao Chiu-yueh
k30.place: Puli (originals at the Paper Dome 'Flow' gallery; outdoor reproductions at the Puli administrative park and Jiji station plaza)
k30.summary:
“Draw, 25” is a Puli exhibition marking the 25th anniversary of the 921 earthquake, with a press conference on 12 September 2024 and the show running to 30 September; it was organised by the New Homeland Foundation with Ministry of Culture support in planning.

Eleven painters returned to the quake-hit area of Puli to work, using paintings to show the contrast between old and new landscapes, alongside an older painter’s post-quake sketches.

The originals were shown at the “Flow” gallery of the Paper Dome, with outdoor reproductions at the Puli Joint Administrative Park and the plaza in front of Jiji Railway Station.
k30.selfDesc: The report says the New Homeland Cultural and Educational Foundation organized the project, with planning supported by the Ministry of Culture.
k30.pedagogicalInsight: Painters returned to the disaster area to work on site and compare old and new landscapes, with no resident co-creation; but “going back and painting 25 years of change” models talking about a place through time depth (after the quake vs now), a method reference for courses on place change. Note: this is work- and curation-oriented.
k30.why: Verified: besides CNA (2024-09-12), TDN Taiwan Life News (reporter Fan Hung-kun, 2024-09-14) independently covers the show, confirming the New Homeland Foundation as organizer, Ministry of Culture support, and 11 artists returning to quake-hit Puli to paint 25 years of change at the Paper Dome; the foundation's official page lists all 11 painters, the Paper Dome 'Flow' gallery, the Sep 12 press event and the run through Sep 30. Upgraded to verified. (daily source expansion, 2026-11-15)

k79.name: Libera Work-Gang: The Galaxy of Discipline — A Research-Creation Project on the Post-war Mainlander ‘Diaspora’ and ‘Suppression’
k79.creator: Libera Work-Gang (project lead: Lin Chuan-kai; lead creator: Hung Wei-ling; collaborators incl. Hsin Pei-yi, Li Chia-hung)
k79.place: Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB), former Air Force Command Headquarters, Taipei
k79.summary:
A residency-based investigation and creation project carried out in 2019 at the Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB), proposed by the Libera Work-Gang. Founded in 2018, the group brings together artists, researchers and popular-education workers; the project lead is White Terror historian Lin Chuan-kai and the lead creator is image-maker Hung Wei-ling.

The project focuses on the situation of post-war ‘Mainlander’ political prisoners. The team notes that about forty percent of White Terror victims were Mainlanders, many of them in the military — at once victims of the authoritarian system and people whose identity is often flattened or used as a political tool. Taking three threads — air force, army and navy — it investigates the spaces, archives and memories of interrogation and imprisonment.

Treating the former Air Force Command Headquarters (the site of C-LAB) as a field, the team used old photographs and the oral accounts of people who had worked there to search for spaces where political prisoners may have been interrogated and held, and produced three moving-image works — The One Who Writes, The One Who Bears Guilt, and Landscape in the Mist — corresponding to the three threads.

Alongside the artworks, the team ran an intensive public programme: reading groups, many themed talks, and a workshop, led by a performance practitioner, in which participants experienced ‘the disciplined body’. It was among the most active residency teams of its cohort, with the largest audiences.
k79.selfDesc: In the group’s own words, the spirit of ‘libera’ (安魂, requiem) is to attend to the resisters who vanished during the Martial Law period — to bring their figures back into the present, and to help people today recover the strength to enter public life. Its method is to re-read ‘Mainlanders’ in a de-ethnicised way, using intensive lectures, reading groups and film screenings to foreground differences of class, ethnicity, culture and wartime experience, and to explore the varied self-identifications of the diaspora. (This paragraph is the team’s / C-LAB’s self-description; the body text relies on independent sources for facts.)
k79.editNote: Classified by the platform as socially engaged art and a residency, on the grounds that it takes White Terror and state violence as its theme and unfolds through an intensive public programme (reading groups, talks, a body workshop). The project lead, Lin Chuan-kai, is a White Terror historian (Dept. of Sociology, National Sun Yat-sen University; born 1979) and is a different person from the similarly named businessman in the news; this has been checked. Reporting varies on the staging details of each film and on the size and make-up of the workshops, so the body text keeps these brief; participants’ role in creative decisions needs further confirmation.
k79.pedagogicalInsight: This case shows how a heavy, abstract history can be turned into something people can investigate and take part in. A few transferable moves: treat a building still in use (the former Air Force HQ) as a field, using old photos and elders’ accounts to ‘excavate’ spaces that can no longer be seen; split a sprawling history into three threads; and use reading groups, talks and a body workshop to turn the audience into co-investigators. A caution: projects like this handle the trauma and dignity of real victims, so keep ‘the team’s own account’ and ‘independent historical sources’ apart, and stay mindful of survivors and their families.
k79.why: Confirmed: the official C-LAB CREATORS 2019 page records that the Libera Work-Gang was founded in 2018 and investigates the former Air Force HQ and the army/navy/air-force history of the White Terror from 1949–1987 archives; the CLABO review (Hsieh Chen-yi, 2020) details the three films and the public programme; the TFAM 2020 Taipei Biennial participant page, Lin Chuan-kai’s university page and the Taiwan Sociological Association bulletin independently corroborate the project lead’s identity, research theme and the team’s collaboration. Several sources of different kinds and from different bodies corroborate one another, so it is marked verified.

k80.name: Keelung Ciao Art Festival 2025 (10th edition)
k80.creator: Organised by the Keelung City Dept. of Cultural Affairs and Tourism; curators Hsi Chen (Taiwan) and Kang Jeauk (Korea); in partnership with Korea's Global Peace Arts & Culture Foundation
k80.place: Keelung (Mountain zone: Keelung Tower, Xin-2 bomb shelter; Sea zone: old Zhengbin Fishermen's Association building; City zone: the Weituohang shopping district, etc.)
k80.summary:
Keelung Ciao is a city art festival run by the Keelung City Dept. of Cultural Affairs and Tourism; in 2025 it reached its 10th year, held 26 September – 26 October. For the first time it was co-curated by Taiwanese curator Hsi Chen and Korean curator Kang Jeauk, in partnership with Korea's Global Peace Arts & Culture Foundation.

The festival expanded across several districts for the first time, in three zones — mountain (Keelung Tower, the Xin-2 bomb shelter), sea (the old Zhengbin Fishermen's Association building) and city (the Weituohang district) — with 15 artist teams in residence and 19 works, plus a market, performances, walking-tour workshops and guided tours.

Curation took a site-specific approach, letting works respond to Keelung's mountain-and-sea landscape, harbour memory and layered identities; the Taiwan-Korea collaboration Tide, Boat, Parting used dance and music to look back at the post-war Korean community in Keelung.

The edition also launched an open-call 'art incubation' scheme, selecting four local teams, and ran guided sessions for schools, new-resident, Indigenous and disadvantaged groups.
k80.selfDesc: Curator Kang Jeauk says he worked from a 'site-specific' concept, thinking about how to fold personal and public narratives into the site, returning art to land and life rather than a static work in a white cube; curator Hsi Chen describes Keelung as a port city nurturing cultural diversity between mountain, sea and city, with the festival as an interface letting that energy flow. (Curators' own account.)
k80.editNote: Classified by the platform as an arts festival and socially engaged art, on the grounds that it takes the harbour's landscape and history as its theme and runs walking-tour workshops and audience-specific tours. As a large festival, residents are mostly audiences/walkers; the depth of residents' co-creation varies by work, so the body text keeps it brief. The edition (10th, 2025), zones and curators are corroborated across several independent sources.
k80.pedagogicalInsight: As a city festival it shows how to make art 'grow in place': a site-specific approach turning a bomb shelter, the fishermen's association building and shipyard remains into the works' sites; walking tours, workshops and audience-specific guided sessions bringing different groups in; and an open-call 'art incubation' nurturing local creators. A caution: in festivals like this residents are mostly audiences or walkers, and genuine co-creation varies by work, so keep 'artists' work' and 'residents' co-creation' apart.
k80.why: Confirmed: Global Views City, CommonWealth's Smile Taiwan, Yam News and The News Lens independently corroborate the organiser (Keelung City Dept. of Cultural Affairs and Tourism), the 10th edition, dates (26 Sep – 26 Oct 2025), the Taiwan-Korea co-curation (Hsi Chen, Kang Jeauk) and the three-zone structure; the post-war Korean-community theme of Tide, Boat, Parting also appears in The News Lens.

k81.name: Sanying Community Co-creation Project (New Taipei City Art Museum)
k81.creator: New Taipei City Government, Dept. of Cultural Affairs / New Taipei City Art Museum
k81.place: The Sanying area of New Taipei (Sanxia as the core field; results shown in the museum's Art Street block)
k81.summary:
One of the community co-creation projects run around the opening of the New Taipei City Art Museum (opened April 2025). Taking Sanxia as its core field, the project carried out on-the-ground fieldwork and visits in the Sanying community, connecting local resources and building partnerships.

Using the rich natural environment around the museum as its theme, it invited artists to lead community residents in a series of co-creation workshops through 'observing, stepping into and embracing nature'.

The workshop results were shown, with public programmes, in the museum's Art Street space.
k81.selfDesc: Per the Cultural Affairs Bureau's report, before the co-creation workshops and curation the project did pre-curatorial research, fieldwork and community visits as a basis; the museum positions itself as a 'museum for all' built on 'participation and co-creation'. (From the official report and the museum's own positioning.)
k81.editNote: Classified by the platform as community art and socially engaged art (fieldwork + artists leading residents in co-creation workshops + an in-museum results show). This case rests mainly on the Cultural Affairs Bureau's official report (June 2024); CommonWealth's coverage speaks to the museum's overall 'participation and co-creation' stance rather than this project, so independent corroboration is thin and it is marked 'to be verified'. Residents' role in choosing themes and curating, and the workshops' scale and audience, are only lightly covered.
k81.pedagogicalInsight: This case shows how a museum can go 'into the community first, into the building second': fieldwork and visits to build relationships, then artists leading residents to approach nature through body and observation, then bringing the co-creation back into the museum. The transferable line is 'fieldwork → relationships → co-creation → display'. A caution: it rests mainly on the official report, with little independent coverage, and residents' decision-making power over themes and curation is barely documented, so it is marked 'to be verified'.
k81.why: To be verified: the project is directly documented in the New Taipei City Cultural Affairs Bureau's official report (June 2024); CommonWealth reports the museum's 'participation and co-creation' positioning but not this project specifically, so independent corroboration is not yet enough. Marked 'to be verified' pending a second independent source reporting on this project directly.

k82.name: Floating Island Scenes — 2025 Taipei Landscape Public Art Project
k82.creator: Taipei City Government, Dept. of Cultural Affairs
k82.place: Yuanshan, Taipei (Yuanshan Expo Park and along Yumen St. by Yuanshan MRT)
k82.summary:
The 2025 Taipei Landscape Public Art Project, themed 'Floating Island Scenes', was run by the Taipei City Dept. of Cultural Affairs, 17 October – 9 November 2025, around Yuanshan MRT and the Yuanshan Expo Park.

Yuanshan carries thousands of years of activity in the Taipei basin — from prehistoric shell mounds and archaeological sites, a Ketagalan settlement, the Japanese-era Yuanshan park and zoo, to the post-war Zhongshan children's amusement park — a landscape that keeps shifting with the eras and accumulates rich city memory.

Continuing the idea 'find the unseen Taipei: bring back hidden or vanished landscapes', it used five landscape works with workshops and walking tours to invite citizens to rediscover this 'floating island'. That year it stood with the Nuit Blanche and the Digital Art Festival, also at Yuanshan, as one of Taipei's three big art events.
k82.selfDesc: The organiser works from the idea 'find the unseen Taipei: bring back hidden or vanished landscapes', using landscape works, walking tours and workshops to awaken citizens' collective memory of the Yuanshan area. (The city bureau's own account.)
k82.editNote: Classified by the platform as public art and socially engaged art (landscape works + walking-tour workshops on the historical layers of the Yuanshan landscape). Dates, place, organiser and concept are corroborated by two independent sources (Smile Taiwan and the Commercial Times / want rich); the individual artists of the five works and the depth of residents' participation are only lightly reported. (The same-venue Nuit Blanche is a separate event, not merged here.)
k82.pedagogicalInsight: A public-art example of turning 'city memory' into a walkable experience: taking a landscape layered from prehistory to the present (Yuanshan) and using landscape works plus walking tours and workshops to let citizens rediscover forgotten strata while moving. The transferable move is 'using a place's time-layers as the lesson'. A caution: sources are mostly event coverage, with little on the works' artists or residents' actual depth of participation.
k82.why: Confirmed: Smile Taiwan and the Commercial Times (want rich) independently corroborate that 'Floating Island Scenes' was run by the Taipei City Dept. of Cultural Affairs, 17 Oct – 9 Nov 2025 at Yuanshan, with five landscape works plus walking-tour workshops, continuing the 'find the unseen Taipei' idea; the individual artists are not listed in the reports.

k83.name: 2024 Formosa North Coast Arts Festival — Walking the Shoreline
k83.creator: Organised by the North Coast & Guanyinshan National Scenic Area Administration (Tourism Administration, MOTC); produced by the Juming Museum; curators Liu Chun-lan (professor, Dept. of Sculpture / Dean of Fine Arts, NTUA) and Yu Wei (art critic)
k83.place: The North Coast (Keelung, Wanli, Jinshan, Shimen, Sanzhi; 21 exhibition sites; the lead venue, the Juming Museum, is in Jinshan)
k83.year: 2024 (lead-in from May; opened 28 Sep – 20 Oct, some works extended to 20 Nov)
k83.summary:
The 2024 Formosa North Coast Arts Festival, themed 'Walking The Shoreline', was organised by the North Coast & Guanyinshan National Scenic Area Administration and produced by the Juming Museum, curated by NTUA sculpture professor Liu Chun-lan and art critic Yu Wei.

Lead-in activities and art workshops ran from May 2024; the festival opened at the Juming Museum on 28 September and ran to 20 October (three large works extended to 20 November), with works across 21 sites in Keelung, Wanli, Jinshan, Shimen and Sanzhi on the North Coast.

Using 'the shoreline' — the shifting intertidal border of sea and land — as its image, it staged a series of projects mixing fieldwork, local participation, community design and the linking of art clusters; over 20 artists were in residence, the lead-in activities alone drew over 250 people, and artists co-created with residents and students from Fuxing High School.

It also invited Japanese community-design expert Ryo Yamazaki to speak on 'arts festivals and community design' across culture, society and environment. Works such as Lu Mu-ren's Mountain-Sea Concerto 25-121 (Juming Museum), Lin Zi-fen's Making Waves (Zhongjiao Bay) and Climate Midway Station (Wanli) touch on marine debris and climate.
k83.selfDesc: The organiser stresses that the festival joins environmental awareness to tourism, with the vision 'local at heart, glory to Taiwan', and that it won a silver at the 2024 London Design Awards (exhibition & events); the curators use 'the shoreline' as a metaphor for an intertidal zone of diverse art-making. (Organiser's and curators' account.)
k83.editNote: Classified by the platform as an arts festival and socially engaged art (a coastal festival mixing fieldwork, local participation, community design and resident/student co-creation). It is a tourism-driven large festival (organised by the Tourism Administration's North Coast office), mostly artists' works overall, with co-creation concentrated in some workshops and student collaborations, as noted in the subjective section. It spans Keelung and the New Taipei north coast; city is recorded as New Taipei (the lead producer, the Juming Museum, is in Jinshan). Organiser, producer, curators, dates and sites are corroborated across several independent reports.
k83.pedagogicalInsight: A festival that treats a whole coastline as a classroom: using fieldwork, art workshops and 'community design' to bring residents and students into the making, then scattering works across 21 landscape sites. Transferable moves are the rhythm of 'lead-in activities first, so residents feel involved before the opening', and putting environmental issues like marine debris and climate into local work. A caution: this is a tourism-driven large festival (organised by the Tourism Administration, stressing a tourism brand); co-creation is concentrated in some workshops and student work, with artists' works dominant overall, so keep them apart when citing.
k83.why: Confirmed: Yam News (opening and curatorial reports) and Storm Media, among others, independently corroborate the organiser (North Coast office), producer (Juming Museum), curators (Liu Chun-lan, Yu Wei), dates (28 Sep – 20 Oct 2024, three works to 20 Nov), sites (Keelung, Wanli, Jinshan, Shimen, Sanzhi; 21 in all) and the 'fieldwork, local participation, community design' approach plus the Ryo Yamazaki talk.

k84.name: 2026 Formosa North Coast Arts Festival — Song of the Tide
k84.creator: Organised by the North Coast & Guanyinshan National Scenic Area Administration (Tourism Administration, MOTC); produced and curated by the Juming Museum (curatorial advisers: Shen Po-cheng, Tsai Wen-pei, Liu Wei-jung / Essence Communication)
k84.place: The North Coast (Juming Museum; Wanli Shanhai Fangyuan; Shimen Baishawan Visitor Center and Laomei; Sanzhi Visitor Center; Shimen Chuhuangkou Farm; spanning Keelung to Tamsui)
k84.summary:
The 2026 Formosa North Coast Arts Festival, themed 'Song of the Tide — Light and Fire Dancing Together', was organised by the North Coast & Guanyinshan National Scenic Area Administration and produced by the Juming Museum, opening on 18 July 2026 at the museum's Taichi Plaza and running to 27 September. It is the festival's 4th edition, and its key visual won a gold at the 2026 Tokyo Design Awards (concept design).

This edition curates around the idea of a 'watershed': rather than following the coastline only, it draws the art route inland through rivers, settlements and mountain-sea paths into living spaces; 'song of the tide' is the echo of waves resonating with life, while 'light and fire' stand for the land's geological energy and spirit.

Works are spread across the Juming Museum, Wanli Shanhai Fangyuan, the Shimen Baishawan Visitor Center and Laomei, the Sanzhi Visitor Center and Shimen's Chuhuangkou Farm, including Yao Chung-han's performance-and-sound work, the ecological installation Water Body by a collective, Tseng Chun-hao with the Lang Jinshan team, and Li Kuei-chih's bamboo-and-steel sculpture; among them, Yang Hsiao-wei and several co-creating artists (Chen Chia-min, Chao Huai-yu, Wang Li-fen, Lai Yu-wen, Liu Shu-chuan) made Twinkle Stop together, in wool and ironwork, at the Laomei bus stop.

The festival also blends music performance, community co-creation and cultural experience; the New Taipei Cultural Affairs Bureau responded for a third straight year with the '2026 New Taipei Art Box' satellite show, inviting five emerging artists to exhibit in Tamsui and the North Coast through 30 September.
k84.selfDesc: The organiser uses a 'watershed' concept to link the North Coast's natural landscape and local culture, stressing art and culture joined to local revitalisation, deep local roots and sustainable tourism, aiming to build an internationally recognisable coastal-art brand. (Organiser's and curatorial team's account.)
k84.editNote: Classified by the platform as an arts festival and socially engaged art (a festival linking the North Coast's landscape and local culture through a 'watershed' concept, including community co-creation). It is a tourism-driven large festival (organised by the Tourism Administration's North Coast office), mostly artists' works overall, with co-creation concentrated in individual works (e.g. Twinkle Stop). The edition (4th, 2026), organiser, producer (Juming Museum), dates (18 Jul – 27 Sep) and work list are corroborated by the official site and several independent reports. It belongs with the 2024 'Walking the Shoreline' (k83) under the 'Formosa North Coast Arts Festival' series.
k84.pedagogicalInsight: Continuing the festival's approach, the 2026 edition scales the curatorial unit up from 'coastline' to 'watershed': rivers, settlements and mountain-sea paths carry works from the shore into inland living spaces. Transferable ideas: using a watershed (not just a single spot) as the curatorial unit, and small-scale co-creation like Twinkle Stop, where one artist leads several co-creators to make a work together in an everyday place. A caution: this too is a tourism-driven large festival, mostly artists' works, with co-creation concentrated in individual works.
k84.why: Confirmed: the official site (Juming Museum curation, watershed concept, work list) and United Daily News, Money Weekly, Yam News and Storm Media, among others, corroborate the organiser (North Coast office), producer (Juming Museum), the 4th edition, the theme, the 18 Jul 2026 opening at the Juming Museum and the run to 27 Sep, as well as co-creation works such as Twinkle Stop.

k85.name: 2023 Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival (2nd edition) — 'Falabidbog'
k85.creator: Organised by the Hakka Affairs Council (executed by the Hakka Public Communication Foundation and L'Brain; project lead Cheng Shih-yu)
k85.place: Hakka villages along Provincial Highway 3 (across 5 counties, 17 townships, about 150 km)
k85.summary: The second Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival ran 24 June - 27 August 2023, organised by the Hakka Affairs Council and themed 'Falabidbog' (Hakka for colourful), inviting people to overturn stereotypes of Hakka culture as plain and conservative. It spanned five counties and 17 townships over about 150 km, and through three strands - art curation, design intervention and a food experiment - gathered 50-plus artists and 21 design teams, about 90 works, plus 35 new Hakka flavours and 60 travel routes.
k85.selfDesc: The organiser frames the festival around three dimensions - art, design and food - stressing the use of design to overturn stereotypes of Hakka culture. (Organiser's and curators' account.)
k85.editNote: The second edition (2023) of the Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival. With the 2019 first edition (k22) it sits under the 'Romantic Route 3 Arts Festival' series. The number of works differs slightly across sources (90/91), noted.
k85.pedagogicalInsight: The second edition puts 'design intervention' and a 'food experiment' alongside art curation, showing how design and food - not just installations - can tell a place's culture. The transferable idea is to make eating and design entry points into Hakka villages too.
k85.why: Confirmed: CommonWealth and Mirror Media independently corroborate the second edition's organiser (Hakka Affairs Council), theme (Falabidbog), dates (24 Jun - 27 Aug 2023), the five-county/17-township/150 km scale and the 50-plus artists and 21 design teams; the number of works (90/91) differs slightly, both noted.

k86.name: 2010 Chenglong Wetlands International Environmental Art Festival (1st edition)
k86.creator: Forestry Bureau (now Ministry of Agriculture) and Kuan-Shu Educational Foundation; Chenglong Primary School and residents
k86.summary: The first Chenglong Wetlands festival was held in 2010 by the Forestry Bureau and the Kuan-Shu Educational Foundation - Taiwan's first environmental art festival themed on wetland ecology. The wetland was once farmland, flooded into roughly 100 hectares of wetland after subsidence and the 1986 Typhoon Wayne seawater intrusion. From April to July 2010, international environmental artists worked with Chenglong Primary School and residents to complete five large outdoor natural artworks from local materials, raising attention to wetland-and-people environmental issues through participation.
k86.selfDesc: Per the Ministry of Agriculture page, the 2010 'A Tribute by Children and Artists' invited international artists with the primary school and residents to complete five large outdoor natural works; local government and industry also helped.
k86.editNote: The first edition (2010) of the Chenglong Wetlands festival. Under the series; the 2025 edition is k23.
k86.pedagogicalInsight: From the very first edition, the primary school and residents were brought into the making, using biodegradable local materials on the wetland site and bringing environmental issues into community education - a founding example of combining 'environmental issue + school + community'.
k86.why: Confirmed: the Ministry of Agriculture page and the newtalk citizen report corroborate that the 2010 first edition, by the Forestry Bureau and the Kuan-Shu Foundation, had international artists with the primary school and residents complete five site-sourced works.

k87.name: 2017 Chenglong Wetlands International Environmental Art Festival — 'Act with Love, Change with Love'
k87.creator: Kuan-Shu Educational Foundation; Chenglong Community Development Association; resident artists
k87.year: 2017 (8th year; residency 13 Apr - 7 May, opening 5 May)
k87.summary: The 2017 edition, themed 'Act with Love, Change with Love', was the festival's 8th year. Seven groups of artists from Scotland, Georgia, the Netherlands, Poland and Taiwan (including the community association) were in residence from mid-April to early May, living in the community and making work from local materials. Residents also re-created a work called 'Rebirth' on the site of the previous year's German artist's piece, continuing their attachment to this place.
k87.selfDesc: Reports note seven artist groups in residence, living with residents and using local materials; residents re-created 'Rebirth'.
k87.editNote: The 2017 edition (8th year). Under the series. Single source, to be supplemented.
k87.pedagogicalInsight: By the 8th year residents could themselves 're-create' on the site of an earlier work, showing a community's build-up from being led to making on its own - a good case for how a long-running festival keeps creative capacity local.
k87.why: To be verified: so far only newtalk (1 May 2017) reports the 2017 'Act with Love' edition's artists and residency; a second independent source is needed.

k88.name: 2022 Chenglong Wetlands Environmental Art Festival (post-pandemic return)
k88.creator: Kuan-Shu Educational Foundation / Chenglong community; resident artist Li Kuei-chih and others
k88.summary: The 2022 edition returned on 24 September after a two-year break. Resident artist Li Kuei-chih made a woven-bamboo installation called 'Seed', inspired by wetland plants, able to stabilise sand and shade birds and fish. Besides installations, local performing troupes gave immersive performances in the wetland's natural setting, using making and performance to renew public attention to wetland-and-people environmental issues.
k88.selfDesc: Reports note the return on 24 Sep after two years, Li Kuei-chih's woven-bamboo 'Seed', and immersive performances by local troupes.
k88.editNote: The 2022 return edition. Under the series. Single source, to be supplemented.
k88.pedagogicalInsight: The post-pandemic edition pairs installation with immersive performance, so the work is not only seen but performed and walked into on the wetland - turning an environmental issue into an experience.
k88.why: To be verified: so far only PTS reports the 2022 return edition (Li Kuei-chih's 'Seed', immersive performance); a second independent source is needed.

k89.name: 2022 Nanhui Arts Festival — 'Where Art Sprouts'
k89.creator: Organised by the Taitung County Government; curator Chen Hsuan-cheng (Dept. of Architecture, Chung Yuan Christian University), with NTTU's Lin Chang-jung and Taitung Girls' High's Kang Yu-ting
k89.place: Dawu, Taimali and Taitung City (along the Nanhui Highway)
k89.summary: The 2022 Nanhui Arts Festival, themed 'Where Art Sprouts', was run by the Taitung County Government and curated by Chen Hsuan-cheng, 21 Aug - late Nov 2022 along the Nanhui Highway. After about two months of fieldwork and site selection, eight teams created eight site-specific works in Dawu, Taimali and Taitung City, exploring the coexistence of nature, life and matter in the Nanhui landscape.
k89.selfDesc: Reports note two months of fieldwork and site selection, with eight teams creating eight works on site along the route.
k89.editNote: The 2022 edition of the Nanhui Arts Festival. The 2026 edition is k42; both under the 'Nanhui Arts Festival' series.
k89.pedagogicalInsight: Having artists do two months of fieldwork and site selection before creating shows the basics of a large landscape festival - 'know the place first, then place the work'. A caution: residents are mostly subjects of fieldwork and viewers, with little on actual co-creation.
k89.why: Confirmed: CommonWealth and Yam News independently corroborate the 2022 edition's theme, organiser, curator and eight teams/eight site-specific works.

k90.name: 2024 Nanhui Arts Festival — 'Realm of Light'
k90.creator: Organised by the Taitung County Government; artists incl. Lai Chun-chun, Tan Su-man (Malaysia), Nitjan Tagivalit, Lin Chun-yung
