k90.place: Taimali, Dawu and Daren, Taitung (seaside sites along the Nanhui Highway)
k90.summary: The 2024 Nanhui Arts Festival, themed 'Realm of Light', opened on 22 August 2024. Three artists were chosen from 44 open-call submissions, with two more invited from South Africa and Taiwan, for five works at seaside sites in Taimali, Dawu and Daren overlooking the Pacific - from day to night echoing Nanhui's light and sea.
k90.selfDesc: Reports note three chosen from 44 plus two invited, five works along the Nanhui coast echoing light and sea from day to night.
k90.editNote: The 2024 edition. Under the series. Single source, to be supplemented.
k90.pedagogicalInsight: Mixing open call (3 from 44) with invited artists and placing works at Pacific-facing seaside sites across day and night - the transferable idea is to make time (day/night) and landscape together into conditions of the work.
k90.why: To be verified: so far only Taiwan Travel (LINE TODAY, 2024) reports the 2024 'Realm of Light' edition; a second independent source is needed.

k91.name: 2025 Nanhui Arts Festival (Zhengxing community, 'Becoming the Shape of a Mountain')
k91.creator: Organised by the Taitung County Government; artist An Chun-shih (Rukai); Sinapayan Youth Station, Zhengxing community, Jinfeng, Taitung
k91.summary: The 2025 Nanhui work 'Becoming the Shape of a Mountain', in the Zhengxing community of Jinfeng, Taitung, was made by Rukai artist An Chun-shih. It extends the community's self-founded 'Sinapayan Youth Station' - a place of cultural transmission and a community living room - into a space joining people and mountain. It is both residents' everyday space and a place for visitors to pause before entering; community leader Kao Kuo-hsi says he hopes visitors stay briefly, respect the place and ready themselves before entering.
k91.selfDesc: Reports note the work extends the Sinapayan Youth Station, a self-founded community living room for gathering youth, transmitting culture and receiving visitors.
k91.editNote: The 2025 edition (Zhengxing community). Under the series. Single source, to be supplemented.
k91.pedagogicalInsight: Making a festival work into a village 'community living room' that also sets the etiquette for entering the community shows how an Indigenous community can use a festival work to shape 'how visitors enter'.
k91.why: To be verified: so far only the Commercial Times (want rich, 2025) reports the 2025 work and the Zhengxing community; a second independent source is needed.

k92.name: 2015 Lukang Jinqiu Arts Festival (1st edition; originally 'Lukang Arts Festival: Jinqiu Hui')
k92.creator: Lukang Gina (Chang Ching-yeh), Changhua Baolu Movement Association
k92.place: Lukang, Changhua (Guihuaxiang art village, old houses and streets)
k92.summary: The first Lukang Jinqiu Arts Festival was held in 2015, originally called 'Lukang Arts Festival: Jinqiu Hui'. After Chang Ching-yeh returned home in 2012 to found 'Lukang Gina' and build community energy through the 'Baolu movement', he took up a residency at the Guihuaxiang art village in 2014 and held the first festival in 2015, curating across the neighbourhood, turning idle old houses into venues and drawing residents in. Its core idea was 'local participation first, then a local festival'.
k92.selfDesc: Smile Taiwan and PAR report Chang founding Lukang Gina in 2012, the 2014 Guihuaxiang residency and the 2015 first festival; the first edition was originally 'Lukang Arts Festival: Jinqiu Hui'.
k92.editNote: The first edition (2015). Under the series; the 2019 edition is k53.
k92.pedagogicalInsight: From the first edition the principle was 'local participation first, then a local festival' - gathering people through a community movement before curating, modelling the order 'organise first, curate second' for a local festival.
k92.why: Confirmed: PAR and Smile Taiwan corroborate the 2015 first edition (originally 'Lukang Arts Festival: Jinqiu Hui'), founded by Chang / Lukang Gina, starting from the Guihuaxiang residency and neighbourhood curating.

k93.name: 2022 Lukang Jinqiu Arts Festival — 'Luojin's Dream'
k93.creator: Lukang Gina Cultural Enterprise (Chang Ching-yeh), Changhua Baolu Movement Association
k93.place: Lukang, Changhua (Longshan Temple plaza, old houses and streets)
k93.summary: The 2022 Lukang Jinqiu Arts Festival was themed 'Luojin's Dream' ('Luojin' is the old name for Lukang), opening at the plaza before Longshan Temple. It continued the practice of holding exhibitions in old houses and shops and using neighbourhood curating and local participation to overturn tourist impressions of Lukang, and added a 'terroir table' across six coastal townships.
k93.selfDesc: Smile Taiwan reports the 2022 'Luojin's Dream' theme, the opening at Longshan Temple plaza and the coastal 'terroir table'.
k93.editNote: The 2022 edition ('Luojin's Dream'). Under the series. Single source, to be supplemented.
k93.pedagogicalInsight: Using a Taiwanese-language theme tied to the town's old name, and extending the 'terroir table' to six coastal townships, shows how a local festival can widen both its reach and its sense of identity through language and food.
k93.why: To be verified: so far mainly Smile Taiwan reports the 2022 'Luojin's Dream' edition; a second independent source is needed.

k94.name: 2020 Keelung Ciao Art Festival (6th ed.) — 'A Day of the Sea'
k94.creator: Keelung City Cultural Affairs Bureau; curator Chen Yen-an (Coastal Production)
k94.place: Around Zhengbin Fishing Port, the Agenna Shipyard and the former Keelung Fortress officers' quarters
k94.summary: The 2020 Keelung Ciao, themed 'A Day of the Sea', was the 6th edition of this northernmost city art festival, curated by Chen Yen-an, 25 Sep - 11 Oct 2020. Fifteen artist groups worked from a time axis, using art, documentation and social participation to unearth the harbour's past, present and future; French artist Margot Guillemot based herself in Zhengbin and made relief masks from residents' portraits, building a face-to-face stage between visitors and residents.
k94.selfDesc: Reports note the edition took 'A Day of the Sea' along a time axis, using art, documentation and participation to tour Zhengbin from morning to night.
k94.editNote: The 6th edition (2020). The 2025 10th edition is k80, under the Keelung Ciao series.
k94.pedagogicalInsight: Making work from residents' portraits to build a face-to-face link between visitors and residents is an unusual move for a city festival - putting 'the people being looked at' into the work too.
k94.why: Confirmed: Smile Taiwan and Supertaste corroborate the 2020 6th edition, curator Chen Yen-an, 15 artist groups and the Zhengbin/Agenna venues.

k95.name: 2023 Keelung Ciao Art Festival (8th ed.) — 'Sea-Light Interface'
k95.creator: Keelung City Cultural Affairs Bureau
k95.place: Zhengbin Fishing Port, the Agenna Shipyard and the tourist fish market area
k95.summary: The 2023 Keelung Ciao, themed 'Sea-Light Interface', reached its 8th year, 28 Sep - 15 Oct 2023 around Zhengbin Fishing Port, the Agenna Shipyard and the tourist fish market. Artists from Taiwan, Japan, Mexico and Brazil made 10 landscape works at Zhengbin - the shooting location of the TV drama 'Port of Lies' - with nightly light shows.
k95.selfDesc: The curatorial idea takes the sea as an 'interface', the meeting of two systems above and below the surface.
k95.editNote: The 8th edition (2023, 'Sea-Light Interface'). Under the series.
k95.pedagogicalInsight: Using one core image (the sea as interface) to unify a whole season's works shows how a single concept can hold a festival together.
k95.why: Confirmed: LINE TODAY and a Keelung school's official guide PDF corroborate the 2023 8th edition, dates 28 Sep - 15 Oct and about 10 landscape works at Zhengbin and the Agenna Shipyard.

k96.name: 2023 Matsu Biennial (2nd ed.) — 'Reddening Through Summer'
k96.creator: Co-organised by the Lienchiang County Government and the General Association of Chinese Culture
k96.place: The four townships and five islands of Lienchiang; front-line sites and villages (incl. the Beigan secret power plant, opened to the public for the first time)
k96.summary: The 2nd Matsu International Art Island, themed 'Reddening Through Summer' (from a Matsu liquor-brewing saying), ran from late September 2023 across the four townships and five islands, continuing ties between island communities and everyday life. Highlights included the Beigan secret power plant, opened to the public for the first time, using light and sound to re-present Matsu's front-line history.
k96.selfDesc: Reports note the 2nd edition used a brewing saying as a metaphor for art fermenting on the islands, continuing community ties.
k96.editNote: The 2nd edition (2023, 'Reddening Through Summer'). Under the series.
k96.pedagogicalInsight: Using light and sound to re-present front-line history in a military space opened to the public for the first time shows how the act of 'declassifying/opening' a closed space can itself be a curatorial event.
k96.why: Confirmed: CommonWealth and a SETN compilation corroborate the 2nd edition 2023 'Reddening Through Summer', organised by the county and the cultural association, and the first opening of the Beigan secret power plant.

k97.name: 2025 Matsu Biennial (3rd ed.) — 'Pah-chhiu: Your Ocean, My Land'
k97.creator: Co-organised by the Lienchiang County Government and the General Association of Chinese Culture; annual-theme curator Nakaw Putun; chief curator Wu Han-chung
k97.place: The four townships and five islands of Lienchiang; front-line sites, bunkers, inlets, power plants and houses
k97.summary: The 3rd Matsu International Art Island, themed 'Pah-chhiu: Your Ocean, My Land' (from Matsu fishing culture; curator Nakaw Putun took 'one mesh feeds one person' as the theme), ran 5 Sep - 16 Nov 2025, 73 days, the longest yet. Organised by the county and the cultural association, it gathered 55-plus teams from nine countries and over 50 works across the islands - e.g. Chen Chieh-jen's work at the Xiju former cinema, Kan Ming-yuan's woven-bamboo piece, and Page Tsou's 'Yellow Croaker Bus', plus 'Ten People, Ten Seas', co-made by local teachers and students with residents of Ogijima, Japan.
k97.selfDesc: Reports call the 3rd edition Taiwan's largest island-hopping art festival; curator Nakaw Putun uses the fishing saying 'one mesh feeds one person' to make art a way of understanding ocean, labour and life.
k97.editNote: The 3rd edition (2025, 'Pah-chhiu'). Under the series. Curated by several area curators; Nakaw Putun is one of the annual-theme curators.
k97.pedagogicalInsight: Using a local fishing proverb as the curatorial core turns labour experience into a way of understanding place; 'Ten People, Ten Seas' models connecting creation to another island community.
k97.why: Confirmed: Marie Claire and Smile Taiwan corroborate the 3rd edition 2025 'Pah-chhiu', dates 5 Sep - 16 Nov, 55-plus teams from nine countries and over 50 works, organised by the county and the cultural association.

k98.name: Toucheng Old Street Culture & Arts Festival (9th ed.) — 'World as Guests'
k98.creator: Goldfish Neighbour (Peng Jen-hung); several transnational artists
k98.place: Toucheng, Yilan (the Toucheng, Wai'ao, Guishan and Dali railway stations, etc.)
k98.summary: The 9th Toucheng Old Street Culture & Arts Festival, themed 'World as Guests', took 'transnational, cross-domain, cross-group, multicultural, co-creation' as its premise across four facets. Goldfish Neighbour worked with the railway and Kamalan Bus on train passes and an art bus, turning the Toucheng, Wai'ao, Guishan and Dali stations into galleries showing transnational artists' work - e.g. Cuban artist Reydel Espinosa's painting fusing Toucheng life with his homeland.
k98.selfDesc: Reports note the 9th edition turned four stations into galleries with transnational artists; Cuban artist Reydel lived in Toucheng with his family.
k98.editNote: The 9th edition ('World as Guests'). Under the series. The year is not stated in the source (roughly 2023 by edition count), marked to be verified; single source.
k98.pedagogicalInsight: Turning four railway stations into galleries linked by an art bus treats a rail line as the exhibition route; transnational artists who have settled locally are both creators and residents, blurring outsider/local.
k98.why: To be verified: so far only Smile Taiwan reports the 9th edition 'World as Guests', without stating the year (roughly 2023); a second source and the exact year are needed.

k99.name: 2021 Luoshanfeng Arts Festival — 'A Thousand Moods of the Wind'
k99.creator: Pingtung County Government
k99.place: Haikou Port beach and the Sea-View Art Museum, Checheng, Pingtung
k99.summary: The 2021 Luoshanfeng Arts Festival, themed 'A Thousand Moods of the Wind', ran 25 Dec 2021 - 1 Mar 2022, run by the Pingtung County Government, with 18 landscape installations at the Haikou Port beach and the Sea-View Art Museum. The Hengchun Peninsula's seasonal strong wind (the luoshanfeng) blows from October to April; works used the invisible wind to leave traces and coexist with the sea and sand.
k99.selfDesc: Reports note 18 landscape installations across the beach and museum, blending with the land and sea and with light and sound.
k99.editNote: The 2021 edition ('A Thousand Moods of the Wind'). The 2025 edition is k56, under the 'Luoshanfeng Arts Festival' series. Single source, to be supplemented.
k99.pedagogicalInsight: Turning a place's 'negative condition' (the wind that cuts tourism) into the protagonist, with wind-driven installations making the invisible wind visible, is a clear case of making a local environmental trait the artistic subject.
k99.why: To be verified: so far only Smile Taiwan reports the 2021 edition; a second independent source is needed.

k100.name: 2023 Luoshanfeng Arts Festival — 'Frequency of the Wind'
k100.creator: Pingtung County Government; in partnership with Japan's Art Front Gallery (Echigo-Tsumari / Setouchi team)
k100.place: Haikou Port, Checheng, Pingtung (Sea-View Art Museum, Wind-Waiting House, outdoor areas)
k100.summary: The 2023 Luoshanfeng Arts Festival, themed 'Frequency of the Wind', ran 15 Dec 2023 - 25 Feb 2024, run by the Pingtung County Government, gathering 17 artists from Taiwan, Japan, Korea and the Philippines for 10 outdoor works, an old-house project and two indoor shows at the Sea-View Art Museum and beyond. It paid homage to Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea and was co-curated with Art Front Gallery (Fram Kitagawa), the team behind the Echigo-Tsumari and Setouchi festivals.
k100.selfDesc: Reports note the edition started from sensing the wind's changes and coexisting with nature, paying homage to The Old Man and the Sea and partnering with Art Front Gallery.
k100.editNote: The 2023 edition ('Frequency of the Wind'). Under the series.
k100.pedagogicalInsight: Partnering with the Echigo-Tsumari/Setouchi curatorial team brings international land-art experience to the Hengchun Peninsula, showing how a local festival can lift its horizons through an international network while keeping its theme tied to local wind and sea.
k100.why: Confirmed: Global Views City and Smile Taiwan corroborate the 2023 'Frequency of the Wind', run by Pingtung County, 17 artists from Taiwan/Japan/Korea/Philippines, the Art Front Gallery partnership and the dates 15 Dec - 25 Feb 2024.

k101.name: 2024 Luoshanfeng Arts Festival
k101.creator: Pingtung County Government; artists incl. Japanese illustrator Yosuke Yamauchi and the Mu-Zi-11 studio
k101.place: Haikou Port, Checheng, Pingtung (beach area, Sea-View Art Museum)
k101.summary: The 2024 Luoshanfeng Arts Festival opened on 20 December 2024 and ran to 2 March 2025, run by the Pingtung County Government, with Japanese illustrator Yosuke Yamauchi among the artists (including a 'FACE SHOP' portrait booth). In the beach area, the Mu-Zi-11 studio's 'Floating Strata' used discarded styrofoam to mimic rocks on flexible supports that sway in the wind, the light plastic set against the weight of environmental damage.
k101.selfDesc: The Central News Agency reports the edition opened on 20 Dec and ran to 2 Mar 2025, with Yamauchi and the beach work 'Floating Strata' using discarded styrofoam to address environmental damage.
k101.editNote: The 2024 edition. Under the series. Single source, to be supplemented.
k101.pedagogicalInsight: Making 'Floating Strata' from discarded styrofoam that sways in the sea wind shows using marine debris as the medium so the work itself carries the environmental issue.
k101.why: To be verified: so far only the Central News Agency (20 Dec 2024) reports the 2024 edition; a second independent source is needed.

k102.name: 2021 Palafang Hualien Jumping Waves Art Festival (1st ed.) — 'Post-Eight Views of Hualien'
k102.creator: Organised by the Hualien County Cultural Affairs Bureau; chief curator Nakaw Putun
k102.place: Hualien Stone Sculpture Museum and the bureau's park; linked satellite venues across the city
k102.summary: Palafang Hualien Jumping Waves is a contemporary visual-art brand launched by the Hualien County Cultural Affairs Bureau in 2021; its first edition took 'Post-Eight Views of Hualien' as its theme. 'Palafang' is Amis for 'to visit', and 'Jumping Waves' is a place name and a way of life from when east-coast people crossed reefs by the rhythm of the waves - both carry a sense of 'coming home'. The first edition showed a themed exhibition at the Stone Sculpture Museum and linked 'eight waves' satellite venues across the city, inviting artists to echo the old Eight Views through contemporary work, with 'local studies' as the curatorial core.
k102.editNote: The 1st edition (2021). The 2022 2nd edition is k103 and the 2024 3rd edition 'Planet Burst' is k27, under the Palafang series.
k102.pedagogicalInsight: Revisiting a set of local classic images (the Eight Views) through contemporary art, split across a museum show and city satellite venues, turns 'getting to know a place' into a walkable art route.
k102.why: Confirmed: LINE TODAY (by VERSE writer Wu Che-fu) and the Hualien bureau's official page corroborate the 2021 first edition's theme, venues and 'local studies' core.

k103.name: 2022 Palafang Hualien Jumping Waves Art Festival (2nd ed.) — 'Breaking Ball'
k103.creator: Organised by the Hualien County Cultural Affairs Bureau; curators Nakaw Putun, Li De-mao, Chang Hui-chun
k103.place: Hualien Stone Sculpture Museum and the bureau's park
k103.summary: The 2022 2nd edition, themed 'Breaking Ball', ran 22 Oct 2022 - 2 Jan 2023 at the Hualien Stone Sculpture Museum. Three curators invited 10 groups of artists to switch viewpoints through different species' 'eyeballs' onto a rapidly changing 'Earth', reflecting on coexistence from volcano and ocean to forest. The opening featured the NSO with singers Ilid Kaolo and Anu; the 'Jumping Waves Bus' again brought children who can't easily reach the city to see the show.
k103.editNote: The 2nd edition (2022, 'Breaking Ball'). Under the series.
k103.pedagogicalInsight: One central metaphor (the breaking ball - different species' eyeballs, and a changing Earth) unifies the season; the 'Jumping Waves Bus' turns gallery-going into educational outreach.
k103.why: Confirmed: the Hualien bureau's official page and CommonWealth Smile Taiwan corroborate the 2nd edition 2022 'Breaking Ball', the three curators, 10 artist groups, the dates and the NSO opening.

k104.name: 2023 Sixteen Coming-of-Age Arts Festival (9th ed.) — Youth Theatre 'Detour'
k104.creator: Tainan City Cultural Affairs Bureau; Lab Theatre (chief director Lu Yi-hsin); TSMC Education and Culture Foundation

k109.name: 2013 'The Tale of Leigonghuo' — first staging in the Kaadaadaan rice field
k109.creator: Residents and elders of the Kaadaadaan (Dianguang) community, adapting and self-performing
k109.summary: The drama version of 'The Tale of Leigonghuo' was first staged in the Dianguang tribe in 2013. In the 1896 Battle of Leigonghuo, the Amis of Dianguang (old name Leigonghuo, for its mud volcano) repelled remnant Qing troops with bamboo cannon; elders adapted the history into a play, first performed in the harvested rice field as part of a community-regeneration series, winning local acclaim with its comic acting, home-made props and invention - the origin of the yearly 'Rice-Fragrance Theatre'.
k109.editNote: The 2013 first drama staging. The 2023 11th edition (by then expanded into the 'Leigonghuo Culture & Life Festival') is k61, under the Leigonghuo Little Theatre Festival series. Single 2013 source, to be verified.
k109.pedagogicalInsight: Elders adapting the tribe's collective memory into a play staged in their own rice field is the most elemental start of a community preserving oral history through theatre - performers and audience are all the tribe's own.
k109.why: To be verified: so far only PeoPo citizen journalism (2013) records the first drama staging; a second source is needed.
